bugs.error_message: User: "Recent actions is not updating as expected. I have to tap in or near the Recent Actions section to force a refresh"
bugs.root_cause: renderFixCard() is only called from renderGame() and the fix-open click handler. scoreChange() and sogTap() call logEvent() (which pushes onto state.game.recent) but then render only renderNudge()/renderOnField(), so the Fix-a-mistake list kept the previous render's markup until an unrelated tap re-ran it.
bugs.fix: Added renderFixCard() to scoreChange() and sogTap(). Rule: any path that calls logEvent() with an undoable kind and does not go through renderGame() must render the fix card itself.

bugs.error_message: User: "Shots on goal is not appearing on Recent Actions"
bugs.root_cause: Two causes. (1) "sog" was deliberately excluded from logEvent's undoable list (commented "informational only - no undo plumbing"), so it never reached g.recent. (2) sogTap logged logEvent("sog",{},id) - the player id went to the archive row's player_id column but not into detail, and g.recent mirrors detail only, so even once listed it had no id to undo against.
bugs.fix: Added "sog" to the undoable kinds, changed the call to logEvent("sog",{playerId:id},id), and added fixLabel/fixConseq/undoFix branches that decrement playerStats[id].sog and log the correction. Verified headless: shot count 1 -> 0 from the Recent actions Undo.

bugs.error_message: Undoing a player's goal left their season goal tally too high — the correcting archive row had player_id NULL, so no per-player aggregate could ever net it out
bugs.root_cause: undoFix() called scoreChange(d.side,-1) without the third argument, so logEvent wrote the correcting goal row with player_id NULL and detail.playerId null. The team score was right (games table) but SUM(detail.d) GROUP BY player_id could not see the -1.
bugs.fix: undoFix now calls scoreChange(d.side,-1,d.playerId). scoreChange only credits playerStats when d>0, so this cannot double-decrement. Verified in D1: the correcting row is {side:us,d:-1,playerId:seed1} with player_id=seed1, and the season leader nets to 2 after 3 goals and 1 undo.

bugs.error_message: .wolf/buglog.json lost entries bug-005..bug-045 — the file came back holding only 4 entries, with mojibake and renumbered ids, after being rewritten
bugs.root_cause: The agent rewrote buglog.json with PowerShell `ConvertTo-Json | Out-File -Encoding utf8`. Windows PowerShell 5.1 writes a UTF-8 BOM (EF BB BF) there. The OpenWolf hook reads the file with JSON.parse, which throws on a leading BOM, so the hook reinitialised the log and began renumbering from bug-001 — discarding the auto-logged working-tree entries, which were never committed and are unrecoverable from git.
bugs.fix: Restored the 4 committed entries via `git show HEAD:.wolf/buglog.json` plus the substantive entries still held in session context (bug-046..051); bug-005..045 (machine-generated hook noise) are lost. Rule: only edit .wolf/*.json with the Write/Edit tools, which write UTF-8 with no BOM. Never Out-File / Set-Content a file another tool parses as JSON.

bugs.error_message: Practice burn-down reported "12 min behind" for a coach who was simply 12 minutes into the first (8 min) drill — only 4 minutes of that was real lateness
bugs.root_cause: behind was computed as elapsed - plannedStart(idx), i.e. elapsed time minus the clock position where the CURRENT drill was due to start. At idx 0 plannedStart is 0, so the figure was just the elapsed time. It credited no progress for time spent inside the drill actually running.
bugs.fix: Added workDone(): finished drills count in full, the running drill counts only up to its planned length. behind = min(elapsed,total) - workDone(), with a separate elapsed-total case once every drill is done. Verified: 12 min elapsed on an 8-min opening drill now reads '4 min behind'; two quick advances read '4 min ahead'.

bugs.error_message: A goal logged during a sync push never reached the archive — the season leaderboard showed the scorer on 0 while the client and the scoreboard both said 1. Its event id survived only as the ofEvent reference on a later correction row.
bugs.root_cause: flushOutbox() loaded the outbox once into `ob`, then awaited each POST and wrote `saveOutbox(ob)` afterwards. logEvent() writes to the same KEY:outbox localStorage key, so any event appended while a request was in flight was clobbered when the stale snapshot was saved back. The events loop also spliced by index rather than by id, so a concurrent unshift/push shifted the wrong rows out. Pre-existing; the goal sheet just fires several events in quick succession and made it easy to hit.
bugs.fix: flushOutbox() now re-reads the outbox after every await and clears rows by id (events) or by key (games/appearances) instead of by position. Verified: the same scripted sequence that lost a goal now lands all events, and GET /stats matches the client's playerStats exactly.

bugs.error_message: User: "The toast text is default Times New Roman."
bugs.root_cause: The app font stack is declared on .wrap, not on body or :root. #toast/.toaststack is a sibling of .wrap (a direct child of body) so it inherits nothing and falls back to the UA serif default. .lockscreen had already hit this and carries its own font-family; .toaststack never did.
bugs.fix: Restated font-family:system-ui,... on .toaststack (with the same comment .lockscreen carries). Verified computed style is 'system-ui, "Segoe UI", Roboto, -apple-system, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif'. Anything else rendered outside .wrap needs the same treatment — better still, move the stack to body/:root one day.

bugs.error_message: User: "The browser alert() pauses the web page, so replace with a custom modal." — every confirm()/prompt() froze the running game clock while it was on screen
bugs.root_cause: 14 call sites used the synchronous window.confirm()/prompt(). Those spin the UA's own event loop: rendering stops, setInterval callbacks do not fire, so the period clock neither repaints nor ticks for as long as the dialog is up — on the one screen whose whole job is a running clock.
bugs.fix: Added ask({title,body,ok,cancel,danger,input}) backed by a <dialog id=askDialog>, returning a Promise (true/false, or string/null for text). Converted all 14 sites; functions that gated on a confirm were split into ask + do* halves, and buildLineup's question moved to the click handler so it could stay synchronous. Verified: the clock advances 9:59 -> 9:56 while the modal is open, and puppeteer sees zero native dialogs across the whole flow.

bugs.error_message: Reset the clock mid-period silently inflates every later sub's playing-time credit, and can make credited time vanish from the ledger entirely
bugs.root_cause: Playing time is credited in periods, not minutes; the clock's only role in the ledger is the split fraction at a sub (editFrac = g.secs/(minsper*60)). resetTimer() put g.secs back to full without touching lu.app, so a later sub was credited against the reset clock — e.g. sub at 4:00 (frac 0.4), Reset, sub at 8:00 credits 0.8 against an entry with 0.4 left. applySub does act.frac -= frac, driving the entry negative, and the frac > 1e-9 filters in appearanceRows/positionTotals then drop it silently. resetTimer also cleared g.onBreak, killing a live break without advancing the period, and was the only clock change in the app that logged no event and could not be undone.
bugs.fix: Added canReset() — false on a break, false when the clock is already full, and false once any entry in lu.app[curPi()] has frac < 1 (the signal that a sub, keeper swap or format switch has already split this period at the clock). Read off lu.app rather than g.recent because that list is capped at 8 and is spliced on undo. resetTimer() now guards on canReset() at entry and again after the confirm sheet resolves (the clock runs on while it is open), logs clock_set (already in logEvent's undoable set, and undoFix already restores detail.from), and no longer clears onBreak. The button moved from .gd-controls onto the clock row as .clock-tag.reset, mirroring the Edit tag; both tags are position:absolute, so hiding Reset shifts nothing. Credited playing time is never rewritten — the confirm copy was already accurate.

bugs.error_message: User: 'When the game starts, why doesnt everyone start at 0?' — on-field chips read 1p/10m at kickoff before a ball was kicked
bugs.root_cause: buildPeriods stamps every lu.app entry frac:1 at BUILD time, and playedSoFar summed app[0..pi] including the in-progress period. The fracs are allocations ('the share you WILL play'), never elapsed time — the clock never touched them; only applySub/applyKeeperSwap/applyFormatOff move a frac, and only at the instant of the tap. The minutes label added earlier that day made the projection assert elapsed time, which was simply false.
bugs.fix: Added LineupCore.playedThrough(lu,pi,id,live,rem) — discounts the period on the clock by the fraction still unplayed, for players currently in lu.periods[live] only; periods after live contribute zero. app.js playedSoFar() wraps it with remFrac() (1 before kickoff, 0 on a break because g.secs is then the BREAK clock). keptSoFar left plan-based on purpose (it backs the one-period-in-goal cap). Verified in-browser across kickoff/mid-period/sub/break/rollover and by 7 simulation tests.

bugs.error_message: First cut of the elapsed formula scored a just-subbed-off player as 0 minutes instead of the 4.5 they played
bugs.root_cause: Used LineupCore.activeEntry() to decide 'is this player on the field'. activeEntry means 'their latest entry with frac left on it' — after a sub the outgoing player's entry still holds the frac they played (1 - 0.55 = 0.45), so it matched, the discount was applied to them too, and 0.45 - 0.55 clamped to 0.
bugs.fix: Test membership in lu.periods[live] instead — that is the actual on-field roster. A player who is off needs no discount because applySub already trimmed their entry to exactly what they played. Caught by a scratchpad probe before it shipped.

bugs.error_message: After the elapsed change the .pp half-pip appeared on almost every on-field chip
bugs.root_cause: ppHtml pipped on isPartial(displayedValue). The pip means 'a sub split one of their periods', but under elapsed timing every number is fractional mid-period, so the test matched nearly everyone and the signal carried nothing.
bugs.fix: Added wasSplit(lu,pi,id), which tests the PLAN fracs per period, and passed it into ppHtml(v,split). Verified: mid-period only the actually-subbed player is pipped.

bugs.error_message: Season simulation: following the ranked #1 sub recommendation every period drifts career playing time 12.4 periods over 20 games on an 8-player 6v6 roster, concentrated on alphabetically-first kids (Ana subbed off 24 times, Ben 22)
bugs.root_cause: renderOnField's off/on lists rank by playedSoFar THIS GAME and break ties alphabetically (nm(a.id).localeCompare(nm(b.id))). The builder front-loads the most-owed into early periods, so at any mid-game glance the most-owed are 'longest on the field' and get recommended off; the freed time goes to back-loaded (career-rich) bench players. On exact-division rosters (24 slots / 8 players = exactly 3 each) there is no spare period for the builder to repay with, so the drift compounds directionally every game. With a spare period (9 or 10 present) the builder repays and season spread stays ~1.5.
bugs.fix: NOT FIXED — documented in test/season.test.mjs ('KNOWN LIMIT' characterization test, fails loudly if the ranking is ever fixed). Candidate fixes reported to the user: (1) break played-time ties by season-owed instead of name, (2) rank by whole-game projection (lu.actual) instead of backward-looking playedSoFar, (3) surface a 'no strong rec' state when the top pair's gap is a tie.

bugs.error_message: S1 (infra audit): GET /api/team/<any 8+ char id>/schedule served the coach's GameChanger family calendar to anyone who knew the app URL

bugs.error_message: C1 (infra audit): putTeam optimistic-concurrency was TOCTOU-racy — two writers reading the same rev both passed the baseRev check and both wrote, silently losing one edit
bugs.root_cause: SELECT rev then an unconditional INSERT ... ON CONFLICT upsert. Two in-flight writers reading rev=5 both pass `baseRev===curRev` and both write rev=6 — the exact lost-write the rev field exists to flag.
bugs.fix: Replaced the blind upsert with a conditional write: guarded `UPDATE teams SET doc,rev,updated_at WHERE id=? AND rev=?` (bound to the rev just read), check meta.changes; changes===0 && no row -> INSERT (first write); changes===0 && row exists -> a concurrent writer won, re-read and return the 409 conflict shape. force / baseRev:null still write unconditionally (UPDATE-by-id + INSERT fallback, no old upsert path). No transaction, no DO. Test 'concurrent writers on the same base rev' drives the interleaving via a stub whose SELECT rev returns a fixed 5 while UPDATE checks the real stored rev.

bugs.error_message: M3 (infra audit): GameClock.alarm() had no outer try/catch — a throwing DELETE FROM push_subs prune made the whole alarm throw, and the DO runtime retries the alarm, re-notifying every phone
bugs.root_cause: Per-endpoint sendPush was guarded, but the prune DELETE was outside any try/catch. A D1 write error there throws out of alarm(), and a thrown DO alarm is retried by the runtime -> duplicate 'Period over' pushes to every subscriber.
bugs.fix: Wrapped the entire alarm() body in try/catch (log-and-swallow via console.log with redact()). Also clear the stored 'team' key when {at:0} cancels the alarm (this.ctx.storage.delete('team')) — tidiness. Uses the new dbOf() helper.

bugs.error_message: C2 (infra audit): every remote-migration route in the repo used `wrangler d1 execute --remote --file`, which fails under an OAuth token (D1 /import, code 10000) — prod once ran with 4 missing tables (bug-140/141)
bugs.root_cause: npm run db:init and the migration files' own header comments all used --remote --file, routing through the /import endpoint that rejects a `wrangler login` token. wrangler d1 migrations apply instead sends each statement through the working /query path.
bugs.fix: Adopted the D1 migrations framework. Folded schema.sql -> migrations/0000_init.sql (full schema, all CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS, idempotent) and DELETED migrations/0001_games_venue.sql + 0002_teams_pass.sql (their columns are already in 0000). DIVERGED from the handoff, which kept the ALTER files: with 0000 being the full schema, keeping 0001/0002 as ALTERs makes a fresh `apply` die on 'duplicate column name' — the very failure the local-verify step is meant to prove works. package.json: deleted db:init/db:init:local, added db:migrate / db:migrate:local. Verified: fresh throwaway-DB `migrations apply --local` ran 10 commands, created all 5 tables + venue + pass_hash columns, and re-apply is a clean no-op. Updated README, anatomy.md, cerebrum. REMAINING (user must run, hits PROD, needs interactive OAuth): seed prod d1_migrations with INSERT OR IGNORE VALUES('0000_init.sql') via --command, then npm run db:migrate.

Historical incomplete archive rows intentionally NOT migrated (wrong numbers cheaper than a prod migration).

bugs.error_message: Season Archive shows 'No events recorded.' for the 9/12 game even though the server returns 8 events and Season Leaders shows the goal.
bugs.root_cause: toggleLogGame guard `!arch.events[gid]` never refetches when the cached value is an empty array ([] is truthy, so ![] is false). A game expanded before its events synced caches [] in localStorage and pins 'No events recorded.' forever.
bugs.fix: Changed the guard to refetch when the cached list is missing OR empty: `(!cached || !cached.length)`. Bumped sw.js CACHE v19->v20 so clients pull the new shell. Data was correct server-side (live GET returned 8 events) — this was purely a client cache/display bug, not a data or backdate problem.

bugs.error_message: Adversarial review: converting a played practice game to real permanently loses its event log (subs, keeper swaps, shots, goals, clock). Same loss class that forced reconstructing 9/12 from screenshots.
bugs.root_cause: logEvent skipped the outbox entirely for a practice game (game.test), and no full event list was kept anywhere durable (g.recent is only the last 8). pickGame's practice->real backfill wrote the game row + appearances but had no events to backfill.
bugs.fix: logEvent now buffers every practice event into a local per-game array g.plog (reset per new game). pickGame conversion moves g.plog into the outbox (game_id-scoped) before queueGameRow, then flushOutbox posts the game row first, then the events.

bugs.error_message: Adversarial review: an in-flight game-row POST can erase a newer snapshot. Outbox.flush deletes the queued game by id after the POST; a score/full-time/iv update during the request is deleted unsent.
bugs.root_cause: The games loop captured the row, awaited the POST, then delete-by-id unconditionally. queueGameRow overwrites games[gid] in place on every change, so a mid-flight update was clobbered. Same race the events path already guarded. Appearances had the same defect.
bugs.fix: Clear the queued game only if JSON.stringify(current)===JSON.stringify(posted); a changed row stays queued and re-posts next flush (idempotent upsert). Applied the same value-match guard to the appearances drain.

bugs.error_message: Adversarial review: an early manual full-time archives an inaccurate interval ledger. iv can say a player played a whole period when their appearance credit is 0.5.
bugs.root_cause: closeGameRow called ivClose (which closed open runs at 1) BEFORE finalizeAtElapsed, and finalizeAtElapsed clips appearances but never touched iv.
bugs.fix: ivClose takes an optional cap (default 1); it closes open runs at cap and drops runs starting after it. closeGameRow now passes 1-remFrac() so iv is clipped to the same elapsed point finalizeAtElapsed banks. No-op at real full time.

bugs.error_message: Adversarial review: a device with the old events-only archive cache never loads the new graphical replay data (appearances/iv), so tracks stay missing. Also postGame silently dropped iv over 40k, and the archive stored player IDs with no historical roster snapshot.
bugs.root_cause: toggleLogGame refetched game detail only when cached events were absent/empty; a pre-track-view cache has events but no arch.appear[gid]. Separately, iv cap was a silent 40k drop and no roster snapshot was kept, so a rename/removal rewrote history.
bugs.fix: Refetch when arch.appear[gid]===undefined too. Raised postGame iv cap to 200k. Added games.roster (migration 0006): queueGameRow snapshots id->name/num, getGameEvents returns it, gameTracksHtml uses it for names/order (falls back to live roster).

bugs.error_message: Coach: the 9/19 (vs Cammell) substitution/playing-time record is wrong — kids who would have sat were sent to play FOR the short-handed other team, but the app logged that as bench time.
bugs.root_cause: Data model has no concept of a player lent to the opponent. With 7 present and 6 on field, the one player off each period was recorded as benched, understating four kids' minutes and skewing season fairness (getPositions SUM(frac)) and the graphical replay (games.iv).
bugs.fix: PARTIALLY REVERTED — do not trust as applied. Manual remote-D1 edit credited lent time back (all 7 full time, reclaimed minutes booked as D) across appearances + games.iv. BUT the live app re-synced seconds later: the 9/19 game is still doc.game (the active game) and is mis-linked to a WRONG schedule slot (doc.game.sched.opponent='Zapata', venue='away', startsAt 10/10/2026). queueGameRow/queueAppearances re-posted from the device, overwriting opponent Cammell->Zapata and venue home->away, and clobbering the appearance rows whose (player,period,pos) keys the app owns (Jeffrey back to 2.49, Oliver to 2.95) while my NEW D-key rows survived — leaving appearances self-inconsistent with games.iv and double-counting risk. ROOT LESSON: never edit the archive for a game that is still the active/syncing game on a device; the app is authoritative and last-write-wins by updated_at. Correct sequence: (1) coach fixes opponent/venue IN THE APP (source = the sched link), (2) game is no longer the current game / device has synced, (3) THEN delete-and-rewrite the game's appearances + iv cleanly. 9/12 Sheffield/away backfill held (that game is not active). See docs/season-data-corrections.md.
bugs.resolution: RESOLVED 2026-09-22. Sequence that worked: (1) coach re-linked the 9/19 game to Cammell/home in the app (fixed doc.game.sched); (2) fixed the stale archive games row to Cammell/home directly (safe once the doc agreed); (3) after coach confirmed the Season tab showed Cammell, did a clean DELETE + reinsert of all 9/19 appearances (32 rows) + iv update via backups/reconstruct-9-19-appearances.sql. Verified all 7 present players full time; Bearett absent; iv consistent. Pre-reconstruction backup: backups/coach-sideline-prod-20260922-102956-pre-reconstruction.sql. RESIDUAL RISK: 9/19 was still doc.game.gid (current game) at write time; if the app re-syncs it as active it may revert the appearances — coach advised to start the next game to lock it in.

bugs.error_message: Season Archive: play-time bars didn't line up with the P1-P4 column headers, and the position letters (D/F/GK) floated midway between two bars so it was ambiguous which bar they annotated.
bugs.root_cause: The .gtrk-bar track used flex (flex:1 1 0 segments) while the P-header and position-letter rows used grid (repeat(var(--q),1fr)); flex/grid free-space rounding diverged so segment boundaries drifted from the header ticks. .gtrk-bar was also an inline span wrapping a block track. Vertically, letters sat 3px below their bar but only 5px above the next player's bar (.gtracks gap:5px) — near-equidistant, hence ambiguous.
bugs.fix: Made .gtrk-bar display:block and switched .gtrk-bar .track to display:grid with the SAME grid-template-columns:repeat(var(--q,4),1fr);gap:3px as the header/letter rows (removed flex:1 1 0 from .gtrk-bar .seg) so all three share identical geometry. Bumped .gtracks gap 5px->12px and .gtrk-pos margin-top 3px->2px so each letter row hugs its bar with clear separation to the next player. Verified with a headless-Chrome screenshot of a harness linked against the real app.css.

bugs.error_message: Season Archive 9/19 P4 bars showed ~23% played for everyone after prod was corrected to a full P4.
bugs.root_cause: toggleLogGame only refetched a game's detail when the localStorage archive cache was missing/empty/pre-track; once viewed, a game's iv/appearances were pinned forever, so server-side corrections never reached that device. (Local D1 was also a stale pull taken minutes before the P4 fix.)
bugs.fix: toggleLogGame now always refetches on open (cached copy still draws first). Re-pulled prod to local. Also .gtrk-row align-items:start + name line-height:14px so names sit level with their bar; sw cache v24.
